prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your neighborhood, budget, the size/age of your home, ductwork condition, and whether you value lowest price, long-term service, or top-tier equipment and workmanship. I can help you pick a great contractor — below are the practical steps and what to look for so you get a reliable replacement.

Quick checklist of what matters most
- Proper sizing (Manual J load calculation) — not just “match the old tonnage.”
- Experienced installers and NATE-certified technicians.
- Licensed, insured, and local (so they handle permits & inspection).
- Clear written quote with model numbers, SEER rating, full scope of work, labor warranty, and manufacturer warranty.
- Ductwork assessment and repair included if needed.
- Start-up and system testing included after install.
- Good reviews, local references, and responsive service/maintenance plans.
- Availability of financing, rebates (Georgia Power/utility), and disposal of old unit.

Questions to ask each contractor (use this as a script)
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide license number and proof of insurance?
- Do you perform a Manual J load calculation for sizing?
- What exact equipment (brand, model, SEER) are you proposing? Why that model?
- What is included in the price (new condenser/air handler/coil, filter media, refrigerant, pads, line sets, thermostat, permits, startup)?
- What are the labor and manufacturer warranties? Are there extended warranty/maintenance options?
- Will you inspect/repair ducts? Is that included or extra?
- Who will do the work (employees or subcontractors)?
- When can you start and what is the estimated duration?
- Can you provide 3 local references from similar installs?

How to compare quotes (don’t just pick the cheapest)
- Compare apples-to-apples: same equipment, same scope (duct work, coil, refrigerant type).
- Look for a complete written quote — vague estimates hide extra charges.
- Factor in warranty length and reputation for honoring warranty claims.
- Check reviews (Google, Yelp), Angie’s List/Angi, BBB. Call references.

Where to find reputable Atlanta contractors
- Look for local authorized dealers of major brands (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem) — brand dealers often provide better installation training/warranties.
- Use local reviews (Google/Yelp), Angi/HomeAdvisor, and the BBB to shortlist.
- Ask neighbors or building managers for referrals.

Red flags
- No Manual J or vague sizing claims.
- High-pressure sales, “today-only” discounts, or insisting on cash.
- No written quote or unwillingness to put equipment model numbers in writing.
- Poor or no online reviews and no local references.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow this to a short list of Atlanta-area contractors if you give your zip code and any preferences (brand, budget, timeline).
- Draft a message/email you can send to contractors requesting quotes and a short comparison template to use.

Would you like me to find a short list for your area? If so, tell me your zip code, home square footage (or number of bedrooms), and whether you have ducts now (or a packaged/split system).
